sources.entry: betterleaks - Finds leaked secrets in git history, directories, and files, from the original author of gitleaks.

summary.one_liner: Betterleaks is a configurable secrets scanner for git history, directories, files, stdin, URLs, and hosted sources, from the team behind Gitleaks.
summary.what_it_does: Scans git repositories, filesystems, stdin, web responses, GitHub and GitLab orgs/users/projects, Hugging Face repos, and S3 buckets for leaked secrets. Detection rules are written in TOML with regex, keyword prefilters, and Expr-based filters that can inspect attributes such as git author, commit message, and file path. Optional validation (-v) makes asynchronous HTTP requests defined in rules to check whether a credential is active, and optional analysis (-a) resolves identity, scopes, and permissions. Rules can also define an explicit revocation Expr that runs only via a separate revoke command, never during scans. The README also describes BPE-based filtering of natural-language false positives, container image scanning, and a Go SDK for embedding the scanner.
use_cases: scan git history for leaked API keys and tokens
find secrets in a local directory or files
check whether detected credentials are still active
scan GitHub or GitLab orgs for committed secrets
audit Hugging Face models or datasets for credentials
scan container images for secrets in layers
add secret scanning to CI pipelines
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> && cd betterleaks && make build
notable: Optional credential validation and identity/permission analysis defined inside rules using Expr and async HTTP
Expr-based prefilters and filters that use git author, commit message, and file path context
BPE tokenization to filter natural-language false positives
Explicit revocation command separate from scans
Scans many sources including GitHub, GitLab, Hugging Face, S3, stdin, and container images
caveats: The main branch is v2 development; until the first stable v2 release, package managers and the Docker latest tag may still provide v1 (migration guide covers release candidates)
Validation and analysis send requests to credential providers, so they are off by default and need -v or -a to enable
